incident.what: A peer session (doc-repo-c0) misread its own REFUSED/ALREADY_CLAIMED claim response as GRANTED (its worktree/branch fields matched the card's prescribed path, which it mistook for proof of identity) and worked the same shared worktree (P:/tmp/hauska-factory-parcel-r2) this lane legitimately held per _queue/log/property.jsonl (GRANTED 12:22:00.656Z; the competing claim was REFUSED ALREADY_CLAIMED at 12:22:18.781Z, 18s later).
incident.detected: 12:30-12:32Z, this lane's own Edit tool call failed with a file-changed-since-read error; investigation found an uncommitted, then committed-and-pushed (commit f83361c, to origin/feat/parcel-r2-juris-stamp) design with two problems: (1) cityLimits stamped as a literal status string 'incorporated'/'unincorporated' rather than the real city_name, discarding landing's actual data and never using absent-verified; (2) a generic --delete-place flag accepting arbitrary place_keys, which the addendum's authorization (exactly the two named orphans, nothing else ever) does not permit regardless of the design-1 question.
incident.resolution: Escalated to the operator twice (worktree-collision handling, then the remote-branch handling once the push was discovered) rather than adjudicated unilaterally. Operator-authorized sequence: (1) quarantine the foreign commit first -- git push origin f83361c:refs/heads/quarantine/r2-unauthorized-f83361c, preserved, never merged; (2) reset --hard + force-push feat/parcel-r2-juris-stamp back to origin/main, executed by the OPERATOR directly (this lane's own permission layer denies destructive git ops even under in-chat authorization -- confirmed working as intended, not a bug); (3) reimplement from the card's own premises.
incident.secondOverlapFound: After merging and deploying the reimplementation and re-running county-wide fill on all six counties, live measurement showed cityLimits wrong-shape counts still present and, on Williamson, INCREASING between two measurements -- the foreign session's Williamson execution (bzfxv, started 12:44:58Z) was still actively running concurrently with this lane's corrected re-run (ph8kw, started ~12:59Z). Cancelled bzfxv (gcloud run jobs executions cancel, confirmed 'Cancelled by user') after a 2-minute stability watch on the git ref showed no further pushes. A parallel check then found the foreign Travis execution (7fnn7) had ALSO still been running (12:44:56Z-13:00:27Z) concurrently with this lane's first Travis re-run (jcllq, 12:59:38Z-13:13:53Z, completed first) -- its trailing write at 13:00:23Z clobbered ~200 rows this lane's job had already correctly processed earlier in its own pass. Re-ran 48453 a second time (nwll6) once the foreign job was confirmed fully dead; this is safe because the upsert (UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL) overwrites cell_state unconditionally on every fresh county-wide pass regardless of prior DB state -- the in-memory 'skip if not unaccounted' guard only prevents double-processing within one pass, it is not a protection against a later run correcting an earlier wrong write.
incident.rootCauseAcknowledged: doc-repo-c0 independently audited its own transcript against _queue/log/property.jsonl, confirmed it never held a valid claim, filed _inbox/2026-09-02_seat-collision-parcel-r2-juris-stamp_incident.md, and stood down to a different card (parcel-r4-companions) without contesting the technical account.
